transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Claire Mendoza (Redwood AE), Jamal Osei (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Aureus VP Procurement), Liam Chen (Head of MLOps), Nora Ruiz (Legal), Samir Das (Security)

Summary (auto): High-level intake. Procurement and legal want clarity on egress charges and KMS handoff. Security wants audit log format and proof of SOC2 controls. SE walked through infra considerations for a private deployment and dedicated capacity fallback.

Topics: MSA/DPA, egress billing, KMS integration, audit logs, pilot acceptance criteria.

Transcript: 
[00:00] Claire Mendoza: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Maya Patel: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks Claire.
[00:07] Claire Mendoza: Great. Quick intros — I'm Claire, AE on Redwood inference. Jamal's our solutions engineer, he'll walk tech.
[00:13] Jamal Osei: Hi all, Jamal, infra and private deployment lead, happy to go through the preflight.
[00:18] Maya Patel: I'm Maya, procurement. Nora is legal, Liam runs MLOps and Samir is security.
[00:23] Nora Ruiz: Hi. We'll try to be concise — we have a couple of redlines up front.
[00:28] Samir Das: And a few security clarifications around keying and audit retention.
[00:31] Claire Mendoza: Perfect. Our objective today is to map the vendor acceptance path: legal, security gates, pricing acceptance — especially egress/ingress — and who owns KMS handoff for privileged keys. Jamal, want to start on the tech implications?
[00:45] Jamal Osei: Sure. High level, there are three deployment options: hosted API, dedicated reserved pool, and private (VPC/on-prem). For Aureus we recommended Dedicated or Private because of data residency and audit needs. With Dedicated you get predictable throughput; Private gives you full network control and customer-managed KMS.
[01:10] Liam Chen: Quick Q — we ran some numbers; most of our inference is short sequences but high QPS, 16 to 32 tokens on average, p95 latency tight. How does that affect egress? We want to make sure egress billing doesn't surprise finance.
[01:25] Jamal Osei: Short sequences help reduce token costs; batching does well here. Egress billing has two components we typically see in procurement: data transfer fees and per-token unit costs. For Private deployments the data egress is internal but there's still audit/log shipping and optionally model telemetry. Those can be scoped out of the DPA.
[01:44] Maya Patel: When you say egress fees, do you mean per-GB network charges or a separate line in your invoice for model outputs? Our finance team wants to separate cloud network egress from Redwood platform egress fees.
[01:56] Claire Mendoza: Good point. We can split them: cloud egress (carrier) vs Redwood egress (service-level per-output fee). We'll send a sample spreadsheet that breaks that down. Jamal, that's the pricing sheet you mentioned?
[02:10] Jamal Osei: Yes, I have a draft. It shows token unit costs, optional prefix caching credits, and a separate line for outbound payload egress (per-GB). I'm also going to annotate where Dedicated vs Private changes cost.
[02:23] Nora Ruiz: On the MSA, we want a straightforward carveout — if logs contain customer data we need to ensure retention windows and encryption at rest. Also exceptions to standard DPA around subprocessor lists, and liability caps need to be restated.
[02:36] Claire Mendoza: Totally. Our legal team usually provides a redline that aligns with enterprise customers; it's typical to have DPA exceptions for audit log retention. We'll send our standard enterprise MSA but add notes where other customers have negotiated.
[02:49] Nora Ruiz: Also, KMS — we need a clear path for privileged key handoff. Aureus uses a third-party HSM provider and we want to ensure Redwood never stores unencrypted keys.
[02:59] Jamal Osei: For Private deployments you can bring your own keys (BYOK) into the VPC; Redwood's control plane can be set to never store private key material. There's a sealed-broker handshake we use with supported KMS/HSMs. Note — some transcripts from earlier calls spelled that handshake oddly, "sealed broker" shows up in docs as sealed-brok or "seal dash broker" so just flagging potential naming mismatches in our artifacts.
[03:27] Samir Das: Can you walk through the audit logs? We need to know fields, retention format, whether logs include raw prompt text.
[03:35] Jamal Osei: Yes — logs capture request metadata by default: timestamps, route, tokens in/out, model version. Raw prompts are optional and can be redacted or hashed prior to leaving the VPC. We commonly provide two formats: JSONL with structured fields, and a compressed daily blob. Retention is configurable; typical enterprise is 90 to 365 days.
[03:56] Maya Patel: If we choose minimal retention, will that affect debugging in production? Liam?
[04:01] Liam Chen: It might. For regression debugging we prefer a rolling 90-day set of prompts hashed and full raw prompts preserved in an internal-only bucket for 30 days. That's a possible compromise.
[04:11] Nora Ruiz: Also, SOC2 — do you have the attestation? We need the latest report.
[04:16] Claire Mendoza: Yes, we have the SOC2 Type II report from last quarter. I'll attach it to the redline packet.
[04:21] Maya Patel: Good. Back to pricing — what about pilot pricing? We want a windowed pilot with a capped spend and an SLA for throughput.
[04:30] Jamal Osei: We usually do a time-boxed pilot with a spend cap and an uplifted priority tier for the pilot. For Dedicated pilots we can reserve a small pool with burst capacity; for Private pilots we provide orchestration scripts and a one-week warmup. Latency SLOs are typically p50/p95 based on the model variant.
[04:49] Liam Chen: On model fallback — if Redwood routes to a cheaper variant during capacity pressure, do we get notified and can we opt out?
[04:57] Claire Mendoza: Yes, rollouts and fallback policies are configurable. We can lock the route to a pinned model version for the pilot to avoid silent quality regressions; Jamal will include the routing policy options in the preflight doc.
[05:12] Samir Das: A security nit — where are tokens stored for streaming responses? We need assurance stream tokens aren't logged by default.
[05:19] Jamal Osei: Streaming tokens are ephemeral in the runtime; we can configure the level of log verbosity and redact any token-like patterns. It's part of the audit policy.
[05:28] Nora Ruiz: On indemnity and liability caps — our counsel won't accept open-ended indemnities. Can you share prior redlines where Redwood compromised?
[05:36] Claire Mendoza: We can. Many enterprise customers have successfully negotiated a mutual cap tied to annual contract value; we'll put examples in the legal packet.
[05:44] Maya Patel: Ok, I'd like a concrete timeline: legal review, tech preflight, pilot start. If we can get the MSA redline by 3/10 and do tech preflight the week of 3/11, we could start a 2-week pilot 3/17. Is that realistic?
[05:58] Jamal Osei: Yes, assuming legal signoff and we get the traffic profile from Liam. The preflight will include a checklist: network connectivity (VPC peering or VPN), KMS vendor confirmation, sample keys and roles for RBAC, and a small benchmark script we run to validate latency/cost.
[06:16] Liam Chen: I'll get the p50/p95 and sample payloads over by 3/12. Also note we're considering a hybrid routing — some requests to hosted low-cost variants and some to dedicated. How does that affect invoicing?
[06:29] Claire Mendoza: We can break out routes on the invoice per model and per capacity type. We'll show a sample invoice line-itemization.
[06:36] Nora Ruiz: A question about data residency: if we do private in region EU-west, can Redwood guarantee no US backups?
[06:44] Jamal Osei: With Private (customer-managed control plane) we can configure region locks and prevent automated backups to other regions. For Dedicated we can set regional tenancy, but control plane backups may flow through our control region — that will be spelled in the DPA. We'll flag the difference in the legal packet.
[07:00] Maya Patel: Any third-party subprocessors? We need full list.
[07:04] Claire Mendoza: Yes, we'll include the subprocessor list; for Private deployments many subprocessors are optional but if you require removal of a specific subprocessor we can discuss mitigations.
[07:13] Samir Das: On-boarding privileged keys — is there a handoff runbook? We need to see the exact steps, the services that will touch the key, and any proofs we can run to validate no keys left in Redwood control plane.
[07:25] Jamal Osei: We'll provide a step-by-step handoff: 1) zero-knowledge key exchange, 2) vault annotations, 3) role bindings - we use ephemeral session tokens, 4) validation script that proves key is only referenced via KMS API and never exfiltrated. We'll include test outputs from prior customers (anonymized).
[07:46] Nora Ruiz: Great. Also please explicitly call out that Redwood won't index or use customer prompt data for model training unless there's an explicit opt-in.
[07:54] Claire Mendoza: That's standard; we'll add the language to the DPA.
[07:58] Maya Patel: Anything on export controls or if we need to restrict model weights leaving region?
[08:05] Jamal Osei: Model weights aren't exported as part of runtime. If you run Private on-prem, weights stay within your network. We'll also supply a FedRAMP/Export-control note in the packet.
[08:16] Nora Ruiz: Ok, I'll need to redline the MSA and DPA. Phraseology around data ownership and breach notification windows is non-negotiable for us.
[08:25] Claire Mendoza: Understood. We'll send a proposed redline and sample DPA clauses.
[08:29] (brief hold / background noise)
[08:40] Liam Chen: One more operational — how does KV cache prewarming work for dedicated pools? We saw a note about "KV cache" in your doc but the formatting was odd.
[08:49] Jamal Osei: Continuous batching and KV cache are part of the runtime; you can prepopulate cache for common prefixes which lowers token cost. For pilot it's optional; we can demonstrate cache hit rate improvements during the preflight.
[09:02] Maya Patel: Ok, recap?
[09:05] Claire Mendoza: Recap: Redwood sends redlined MSA + DPA examples, SOC2 report, subprocessor list, and pricing/egress spreadsheet by 3/07. Jamal sends tech preflight doc and sandbox instructions by 3/08. Aureus provides traffic profile and KMS vendor choice by 3/12. Legal will aim to return redlines by 3/10. Pilot target start 3/17 if legal + tech greenlight.
[09:31] Nora Ruiz: We'll try to meet those dates. Note I'll add flagged clauses inline with proposed language.
[09:36] Claire Mendoza: Thanks Nora. Anything else from Aureus?
[09:39] Samir Das: No, just the audit log schema and the key-handoff runbook.
[09:43] Claire Mendoza: Great — we'll share those. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet.
[09:48] (meeting ends)

Notes on imperfect transcription: speaker labels sometimes merged (e.g., "MayaPatel" captured as "Maya P"), product names recorded as "Redwood dedicate" or "Redwood pri-vate" in a few sections; timestamps approximate.
